name: Confidential transgender dating app (Flippa listing 13369500; public listing does not disclose the app name)
demand: Search volume: unverified; I found no auditable monthly keyword count. Flippa says detailed traffic is behind signup, and its public page does not expose the underlying traffic report: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential. Population indicators: the Williams Institute estimated 1.6 million transgender people age 13+ in the US, including 1.3 million adults, in 2022: https://williamsinstitute.law.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/Williams-Institute-Data-in-Review-2022.pdf. ONS guidance published in 2025 says its Census 2021 estimate of 0.54% of England and Wales residents age 16+ gives an indication of population size but should not be treated as precise: https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/culturalidentity/genderidentity/articles/census2021genderidentityestimatesforenglandandwalesadditionalguidanceonuncertaintyandappropriateuse/2025-03-26. Store and user signals are mostly operator claims: My Transgender Date reports 2.6 million profiles and 65,000 monthly active users, while its Google Play app shows 100K+ downloads; these figures are not independent validation: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en_CA&id=com.mytransgenderdate.app. HER reports 14 million+ users on its App Store listing and 15 million+ on its website, for a broader queer audience: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/her-lesbian-queer-lgbtq-dating/id573328837 and https://weareher.com/trans-dating/. The Flippa listing itself claims 1M+ registered users and customers in 66+ countries, but does not expose supporting data publicly: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential.

Butterfly lists US VIP purchases of US$9.99, $29.99, $71.99, $107.99 and $143.99; the public page does not map each price to a subscription duration: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/butterfly-transgender-dating/id1477032708?platform=tv.

platform_risk: High. The seller claims 100% organic acquisition, making search ranking and app-store visibility important dependencies; public traffic evidence is gated behind signup: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential. Apple requires filtering, reporting, blocking and contact details for UGC apps and may remove apps whose use violates its UGC rules: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/uk/. Google Play requires ongoing UGC moderation plus reporting and blocking: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9876937?hl=en. Ofcom identifies dating services as user-to-user services and says the Online Safety Act can apply to services with UK links, including those based abroad; child-access and safety duties depend on the service assessment: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/cy/online-safety/illegal-and-harmful-content/dating-and-social-discovery-know-the-online-safety-risks-rules-and-how-to-comply and https://www.ofcom.org.uk/online-safety/protecting-children/protection-of-children-duties-under-the-online-safety-act. Dating profiles may reveal sex-life or sexual-orientation data, which the ICO treats as special-category data; gender identity also requires careful handling: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/lawful-basis/special-category-data/what-is-special-category-data/ and https://ico.org.uk/action-weve-taken/complaints-and-concerns-data-sets/data-security-incident-trends/glossary-of-terms/data-type/. Google Ads restricts advertiser-curated audience targeting for sensitive categories including transgender identification and sexual orientation: https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/143465?hl=en-uk.
defensible_asset: Potential network effect, not yet proven as a transferable moat. The seller claims 1M+ registered users, 2,800 active subscribers, 7% overall churn, six years of age and reach in 66+ countries, but active-member counts by geography, matching liquidity, churn period and cohort retention are undisclosed: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential. A dating network could be valuable where enough relevant members are active locally; that is an inference, not evidence that the claimed base is active or retained. No compiled proprietary dataset or maintained rules engine is evidenced. The database is listed as included, but should not be valued as freely reusable without verifying user rights, notices and lawful transfer.
build_effort: Buying avoids building two apps and a backend from scratch, but ongoing operating effort appears high for an AI-led solo owner. The seller says a remote contractor team runs the service, costs are about $10,000/month, and the owner handles strategy and contractor coordination; no hours, team contracts or support/moderation workload are disclosed: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential. AI agents could help with reporting, routine support triage, SEO content drafts and engineering assistance. Safety escalations, account appeals, privacy requests, contractor oversight and store releases still require accountable human review, given platform moderation requirements and UK safety/data obligations: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9876937?hl=en, https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/individual-rights/individual-rights/right-to-erasure/, and https://www.ofcom.org.uk/online-safety/illegal-and-harmful-content/dating-and-social-discovery-know-the-online-safety-risks-rules-and-how-to-comply.
channel: For user acquisition, use public SEO, app-store optimization, contextual or intent-based ads that comply with platform policy, and opt-in partnerships. Do not target advertising audiences based on transgender status or sexual orientation where the ad platform restricts it; Google explicitly restricts advertiser-curated audiences for these sensitive categories: https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/143465?hl=en-uk. No cold email, SMS, DM or calls. Check applicable local privacy and advertising rules before entering each country.
owner_hours_per_week: unverified. The seller says minimal daily involvement and describes strategy/contractor coordination, but gives no weekly hours or handover evidence: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential.
automation_reason: Analyst estimate, not measured operating data. The listing identifies a remote contractor team rather than an AI-agent operation and discloses no task-hour breakdown. Agents could take some routine content, analytics, admin and support triage; ongoing moderation, escalations, legal accountability and contractor coordination limit the share that can safely run without people. Google Play and Apple require active UGC safeguards: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9876937?hl=en and https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/uk/. At 35% estimated automation, the evidence does not support the >=50% requirement.
listing_check: Revenue: Flippa says it vetted revenue, expenses and traffic, but no source statements or reporting dates are visible publicly; seller claims conflict ($350K+ title versus $380K narrative TTM, and $13,225 monthly profit on the card). Churn: 7% is displayed, but period, denominator and cohort data are unverified. Owner hours: unverified; 'minimal daily involvement' does not establish <=5 hours/week. Price/profit: card shows $259K and $150K with a 42% reduction badge, so $150K appears to be the reduced price but should be confirmed. At $150K, annualized card profit of $13,225 x 12 implies about 0.95x profit; at $259K it implies about 1.63x. Seller narrative separately says $389K price against $155K TTM profit, about 2.5x. The narrative price and current card do not reconcile. Transferability: seller says iOS/Android apps, backend, database, domain and SEO assets are included, but app identifiers, account status, payment setup, user-data rights, contracts and purchase terms are not public. Apple provides a formal app transfer path, with criteria and subscription-specific steps: https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/transfer-an-app/overview-of-app-transfer/. Google transfers app users, statistics and subscriptions through its formal process, subject to account and payments requirements: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6230247?hl=en. Seller dependence: the listing describes contractor operations and owner strategy/coordination, but hours, contractor retention and key-person dependencies are unverified. Overall: not acquisition-ready on public evidence; price and operating claims need reconciliation.
moat_assessment: Conditional, medium-to-weak until diligence verifies local active-member density and retention. A six-year claimed network and 1M+ registered accounts could create network effects, but registrations are not active liquidity; the 2,800 subscriber and 7% churn figures have no visible period or cohort proof. No independent proprietary-data or rules-engine moat is evidenced. Switching costs are likely limited by users being able to join multiple dating apps; that is an assessment, not a verified listing fact. Treat the database as a compliance-sensitive asset, not a freely transferable data moat, until rights and transfer basis are checked: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential and https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/lawful-basis/special-category-data/what-is-special-category-data/.
desk_test: No-cost, one-day pre-offer kill test through the active Flippa listing's NDA/data-room route: reconcile the latest 12 months of Apple, Google and payment-processor proceeds to bank deposits; obtain the exact reporting end date; reconcile the 7% churn definition to subscriber cohorts; inspect MAU/active profiles by country and support/moderation workload; and identify app IDs and transfer eligibility. If the seller cannot provide those records promptly or the figures do not reconcile, stop before an offer. This tests acquisition evidence without customer cold outreach.
red_flags: Public page hides app identity and detailed financials/traffic behind signup; no app-store IDs are exposed, so the asset cannot yet be matched to public reviews, ratings, privacy declarations or transfer status. Financial claims conflict: $350K+ versus $380K TTM revenue; $155K TTM profit versus $13,225 monthly card profit; $389K narrative price versus the apparent $150K reduced listing price. Churn is undefined. 1M+ registered users does not establish active local network density. Owner hours and seller dependence are unverified. Contractor costs of about $10K/month and a human contractor team challenge the <=5h/week and >=50% AI-work constraints. Sensitive user data, app-store UGC rules and UK online-safety obligations add material operating work: https://flippa.com/13369500-profitable-transgender-dating-app-ios-android-100-organic-traffic-5-year-record-1m-users-350k-ttm-revenue-massive-seo-aso-ugc-potential, https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/uk/, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9876937?hl=en, and https://www.ofcom.org.uk/cy/online-safety/illegal-and-harmful-content/dating-and-social-discovery-know-the-online-safety-risks-rules-and-how-to-comply.
